## What's new in 0.1.0
This is Campertron's first stable version. Its programs are built from the same code as 0.1.0-preview.2; apart from the version number, nothing in them has changed since that preview, so 0.1.0-preview.2 users only need to replace their downloads. If you are new to Campertron, "Campertron 0.1.0 at a glance" below sums up what it does; if you are upgrading from an older version, "Upgrading from an earlier version" lists what changed for you.

### The first stable version
- The container image now also gets the tags `0.1` and `latest`, which the beta and preview images never had. Use the tag `0.1.0` if you want to stay on exactly this version.
- The README now says how each download is tested before a release (under "System requirements"), and a new section, [Quality and release process](https://github.com/ShaunAnthonyHathaway/Campertron#quality-and-release-process), describes who maintains Campertron, what every change and every release is checked with, how to check a download, the limits of those checks, and what to include in a bug report.

### Campertron 0.1.0 at a glance
- **It watches recreation.gov for campsites that open up** at the campgrounds you choose. Each search is a small settings file: the campground, the dates (days or months ahead, specific dates, a range, or up to a date), the days of the week, the number of consecutive nights, and filters.
- **The console** shows the results in the terminal or as a web page, or emails them. In email mode it keeps running, waits a minute between checks and emails only openings it hasn't reported before. It is also available as a container image for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`, which runs in email mode.
- **The GUI** has four tabs: **Searches** creates and edits your search files, **Results** runs them and shows the openings with a link to each campsite's booking page, **Settings** edits `General.yaml` and `Email.yaml` (**Campertron**) and sets a System, Light or Dark theme (**System**), and **Campgrounds** looks up a campground's ID and details **By Park**, **By City** or **By State**.
- **Filters:** each of the eight include and exclude lists (equipment, campsites, site attributes and campsite types) keeps or leaves out a campsite that matches **any** of its values. In the GUI you check the values from the campground's own data, read from the campground list on your computer, or type your own. A search matches its values **Exact**ly or as **Contains**: new searches use Exact, and a search file without a `filterMatching` setting uses Contains. Campsite names always match exactly.
- **Your files stay yours:** saving from the GUI changes only the lines you edited; your comments, blank lines, order and formatting stay as you wrote them, and so do values the campground doesn't have. Each save keeps the previous version as a `.bak` file, the GUI doesn't write over a change another program made in the meantime, and a file it can't edit safely opens read-only with the reason.
- **Openings are not reservations:** Campertron finds openings and links to them; you book on recreation.gov, and an opening can be gone before you do.

## Upgrading from 0.1.0-preview.2
- **Desktop:** extract the new archives and use them instead of your old Campertron folders. Your settings, searches, campground list, `Camp.History` and theme choice are kept and need no changes, and the programs behave as before.
- **Docker:** change the image tag to `0.1.0` (or to `0.1` or `latest`) and recreate the container with the same `/config` and `/cache` mounts.
- To check your download, use the checksums and build attestations described under "Verify your download" below.

## Upgrading from an earlier version
Your settings and searches are kept, and the desktop and Docker steps are the same as above. Some behavior changed in the versions you skipped; the "Upgrading" sections of the [0.1.0-preview.2](https://github.com/ShaunAnthonyHathaway/Campertron/releases/tag/v0.1.0-preview.2) and [0.1.0-preview.1](https://github.com/ShaunAnthonyHathaway/Campertron/releases/tag/v0.1.0-preview.1) notes give the details. The changes most likely to affect you:
- **Filters with several values (since 0.1.0-preview.2):** an `excludeEquipment`, `excludeAttributes` or `includeCampsiteType` list with two or more values now matches a campsite that has any of them, so a search can find different campsites. Check those lists in the GUI's Searches tab; nothing in the file changes unless you save it.
- **Matching (since 0.1.0-preview.2):** your existing searches keep Contains matching because they have no `filterMatching` setting. To match values exactly, choose **Exact** under **Matching** in the Searches tab.
- **Settings problems are found at the start (since 0.1.0-preview.2):** in email mode an incomplete `Email.yaml`, and a few settings that used to make a search hang or fail, now stop Campertron at the start with the file's name and exit code 1. The GUI's Settings and Searches tabs show the problem.
- **The first start of 0.1.0-preview.2 or later** adds an index to `RecreationDotOrg.db`, which takes about 35 MB more disk space.
- **If none of your search files has `autoRun: true` (since 0.1.0-preview.1):** Campertron searches nothing; it no longer replaces `ZionConfig.yaml` with the example and runs it. Set `autoRun: true` in the searches you want to run.
- **Linux data folder (since 0.1.0-preview.1):** if your `CampertronConfig` folder was in the folder you started Campertron from, move it to `~/.local/share` (or `XDG_DATA_HOME`) before you start this version.
- **Processor (since 0.1.0-beta.10):** on Intel and AMD computers, this version needs a processor with the x86-64-v2 instruction set, which practically every PC from the last decade has; see "System requirements" in the README.

## Known limitations
- **The GUI on Windows and macOS.** Before publishing, the GUI is started on Windows and macOS and runs its built-in checks there, including its light and dark themes and a campground's filter values. Those checks don't cover how the tabs look, keyboard use or screen readers, or whether **System** follows the theme setting of Windows and macOS.
- **Console on Windows and macOS.** The console's layout, colors and menu had a manual visual check on Windows, not a complete test, and haven't been tried on macOS.
- **Checking hundreds of filter values before saving.** Each change re-checks every value you added since the last save, so after checking all 360 campsites of a large campground, each further change takes about a second until you save.
- **The Results tab can take a few minutes when recreation.gov doesn't answer.** A month is asked for up to three times, with a wait of 30 seconds after a failed request, before it is listed as "not checked". **Cancel** ends the wait at once.
- **Searching one campground for the first time in two Campertron programs at once** can make one of the searches stop with an error, because both prepare the campground's site details at the same moment. This has not been seen in testing; if it happens, run the search again.
- **Email mode keeps running without any search to run.** If none of your search files has `autoRun: true`, email mode warns once and then reports "0 searches" at every check.
- **Email clients not yet checked.** The results page was checked in Chrome and Firefox on Linux, but no test email was sent, so its appearance in Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail is unverified. Each email contains the page twice (as the body and as the attachment), so a search with thousands of results can make a large email that some providers may reject.
- **Your email password is stored as plain text** in `Email.yaml`, which gets your system's usual file permissions when Campertron's first start creates it, and the README's Docker steps make the settings folder writable for every user of the computer. This matters on a computer that other people can sign in to.
- **The included campground list is recreation.gov's data of November 10, 2026.** Campsites added since then are not reported until you refresh the list (see "Keep the campground list up to date" in the README).
- Avalonia, the GUI's UI framework, lists 32-bit Windows (`win-x86`) as a commercially supported platform only and doesn't list 32-bit ARM Linux desktops (`linux-arm`). The 32-bit Windows downloads are started on 64-bit Windows before publishing, not on a 32-bit system, and the `linux-arm` downloads are built but not started.
